source_row.society: British Society for Surgery of the Hand
source_row.extraction_instructions: LightMedia CMS (same family as Vascular Society and BAUS), server-rendered. /about/events is a YEAR view of div.date_row rows (dates | title link | location) whose classes give the category (scientific_meeting, instructional_course, bssh_event, badged_event, date_passed); list_shells_override walks the current year plus /about/events/date/<YYYY>/ for two more years and keeps upcoming rows. Detail pages have header h1 + two bold lines (dates, venue) and tab panes; the Scientific Meeting page has a full-meeting/one-day fee matrix, numbered pre-congress workshops with 'Course Registration fee: £N' and a 'VENUE:' block, courses state fees as prose ('Early Bird Registration - £250 - Book before 1/9/26') or on an external bookwhen.com page (fees and '2 days' duration read there). Gotcha: header venue is often just a city, so the VENUE block / 'at <place>, <postcode>' prose is used to upgrade it.

registry_comment: BSSH events: LightMedia year-view listing (current + 2 years), bespoke fee-matrix/prose/bookwhen fee parsing, 3-way event_type from row class

concerns: Coverage checklist: #1 multi-day ranges parsed from header/listing (incl. 'D Mon YYYY HH:MM - D Mon YYYY HH:MM'); #2/#5 fees on the organiser's bookwhen.com page followed one hop (Pulvertaft course: £580/£740 and the real '2 days' duration, which the BSSH header omits); #3 no fee images seen; #4 no same-site registration sub-pages exist; #6/#7 abstract submission is left to the pipeline merge step (Scientific Meeting says 'Abstract submission has now closed').

Fees are empty for BSSH Instructional Course Nerve and Tendon (Feb 2027), Hand & Wrist Arthroplasty Course (May 2027, Manchester) and the Autumn Scientific Meeting 2027 (Manchester Central): the pages say 'More information will be available later'. Justified against page text, side links and external links (none for these three).

Pulvertaft Wrist Fracture Fixation Course page (19 Mar 2027) says 'followed by' / '2-day' about the sister course, so coverage_checks prints a SINGLE_DAY_SUSPECT false positive; the wrist course really is 1 day (bookwhen: '1 day').

The Scientific Meeting pre-congress workshops are emitted as extra fee tiers on the parent row ('Pre-Congress Workshop · <name>'); closed/sold-out workshops are skipped. Dinner/golf extras are not emitted. Registration pages are on bssh.eventsair.com (JavaScript) and were not read; the public fee matrix on bssh.ac.uk is the source.
Only members' rates that bssh.ac.uk itself prints are stored; nothing is behind a login.

Text-LLM chain on 2026-10-21: nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b and meta/muse-glimmer-30b both answered 404 'gone', so the harness descriptions/specialties came from openai/gpt-oss-20b. Descriptions and specialty have deterministic backstops (first real paragraph; per-society default specialty), so extraction does not depend on the LLM. The probe_models job will go red until the chain is rotated.

specialty_classifier.classify_specialty is deliberately NOT used as the backstop: on single-specialty societies it returned wrong labels (Cardiology/Oncology/GP Training for hepatology webinars). The backstop is the society's own specialty constant when the LLM returns None.

Shared-helper wishes (not changed, per rules): pricing_tables.parse_pricing_tables keeps only the LAST price column when the header names are not timeframes (BSSH Scientific Meeting 'Full meeting | One day' lost the full-meeting rates), drops the category column of [Ticket | Category | Price] tables (BAUS), and can take a nearby sentence as the section name ('Registration fees do not include'). Each extractor carries a small local table helper instead (matrix_tiers / ticket_tiers / rowspan_tiers / external_fee_hop, duplicated inline per file).
coverage_checks SINGLE_DAY_SUSPECT / PRICE_TEXT_ON_PAGE warnings that remain in the harness are explained per source below; none is a missed fee or date on the event's own page.

2026-10-21 hardening: external hops (bookwhen/EventsAir/organiser sites) use safe_fetch.fetch_validated (30 s deadline, 2 MB cap), no browser fallback; host checks use urlparse().hostname. Society-own pages keep fetch_html.
